Lathea finds and treats him as hostile exploration parties begin hunting them. The pair eventually reach a spiral of floating islands that Hadjar somehow remembers how to cross. The pursuing immortal tries to force the barriers and destroys much of the structure. His attack summons a colossal flaming guardian to restore balance. Hadjar and Lathea survive the initial clash, but the guardian, the immortal, and the remaining cultivators now stand between them and the summit.

Lathea holds back the immortal and his followers while Hadjar reaches the summit, ignoring its treasures to enter the first temple. A reflection shows the chained Nameless as the Black General, after which Hadjar wakes holding a stone marked Therna. The stone dissolves into his hand and the anomaly starts to collapse. Hadjar returns to Lathea, but the immortal kills his own followers and allies to erase all witnesses before demanding the temple object. Hadjar and Lathea fight him together and manage to wound him, though his final technique immobilizes them. A dying Lesket woman breaks an artifact, seizes the weakened immortal, and carries them both into a rift where they are destroyed. Hadjar and Lathea return to the caravan site almost immediately after the original disaster, despite their long experience inside the anomaly. They choose to detour to the Lesket clan so the woman's family will know that she died honorably. The Therna stone remains absorbed in Hadjar's palm, and its purpose is still unknown.

Hadjar and Lathea report the Lesket expedition's destruction and reach the clan capital, where the clan head's pacifist younger son receives them. During a tense audience, Hadjar recounts the final survivor's sacrifice and insists that her funeral honor the women among her ancestors. The clan head offers information about a possible route into the true North, but first tries to place Hadjar in a compromising first-blood duel against his eldest son. Lathea converts the private trap into a public contest. Before the duel, she and Hadjar discuss their unexplained sense of long familiarity and Hadjar's desire to avoid needless killing. A separate scene reveals that the queen of cold and darkness is summoning her imprisoned brother, the wolf of darkness, to a coming war and ordering him to kill the reborn vessel of Myristal. In the public duel, Hadjar neutralizes the eldest son's two-blade style, breaks both weapons, and stops at his throat with only a superficial cut. The defeated son accepts the lesson and calls Hadjar master.

Hadjar bargains for Lesket support rather than personal payment. The clan head provides a large body of warriors for the northern expedition but refuses to take a public position against the Twilight Secret Sect. At Lathea's insistence, the clan head's younger son joins the party as its mage. A white-turbaned wanderer coordinates the force. Hadjar tests the mage's ability to protect the expedition, first by attacking him and then by forcing him to confront a celestial thunderbird. The mage casts with exceptional speed, combines multiple elements, and traps the creature alive. Hadjar completes the kill without endangering him and gives him the thunderbird core as the reward he earned. Their disagreement over violence remains, but the mage wins Hadjar's trust. As the expedition approaches the mountain foothills, Lathea reveals a recurring childhood dream in which she dies defending an icy mountain. The group seeks one night's supplies and route information from a northern village before continuing.

The village chief grants the expedition shelter under strict hospitality customs, refuses payment, and requires the soldiers to leave at dawn. During the night, Hadjar dreams of a deceased friend who warns that Lathea needs him and offers a clue from the threshold of the ancestors' realm. Hadjar wakes poisoned amid a Raven Sect assault. The attackers burn the village and massacre both residents and expedition members while the campaign coordinator fights sect swordsmen. The village chief is mortally wounded after admitting the travelers. A raven bearing the Black General's voice directs Hadjar to use his dead friend's clue. Hadjar draws the surrounding fire and wind into himself, burns the poison from his body, and gains a dangerous but unstable command of flame alongside wind. He stops an incoming attack, but more than thirty Raven Sect fighters surround him. Lathea and the Lesket mage are missing, and the purpose and full scale of the ambush remain unclear.

Hadjar combines Therna, wind, and his temporary command of flame in an overwhelming sword attack. He kills the Raven Sect force's armored officer and eliminates the remaining raiders, while refusing to let his weapon absorb their Black General fragments because doing so could strengthen the hostile presence bound within him. The borrowed union of wind and fire fades as soon as the fight ends. The wounded campaign coordinator points Hadjar north, indicating that the missing members of the expedition were taken in that direction. Exhausted from the poison, transformation, and battle, Hadjar follows the abductors toward the mountains. Lathea and the Lesket mage remain missing, the village has been devastated, and the surviving condition of the wider expedition is not established.

Hadjar finds the Lesket mage alive but tortured in a canyon, guarded by the Raven Sect master's seventh disciple. The disciple reveals that an infiltrator poisoned Hadjar and that Lathea left Hadjar's coach before the attack. His spirit-incarnation sword technique overwhelms Hadjar. The mage sends Hadjar the thunderbird core, and the Black General instructs him to break it and complete his white lightning step. Hadjar combines that step with Star Flash and a wind sword, wounds the stronger disciple, and forces him to withdraw. He finds wolf tracks showing that Lathea was dragged farther north, then collapses. A northern host rescues Hadjar and the mage. Hadjar awakens seven nights later, still too weak to pursue. The mage's body survives, but his soul is lost among ancestral memories and may not return. The host has heard the dogs of the wolf of darkness and believes they are holding Lathea alive as bait for Hadjar. Her rescue, the mage's recovery, the northern campaign, and the war against the Raven Sect remain open.

characters.description: A former general and accomplished swordsman detained with his companions by the Twilight Secret Sect. Publicly recognized as the Mad General, he may also be the sect's best chance of dealing with the approaching Raven Sect.
characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.name: Lathea

characters.description: A composed former associate of the Twilight Secret Sect's head and a strategic ally to Hadjar. While the party is detained, he argues that Hadjar offers a better prospect for negotiating with the force approaching the sect.
characters.name: Abraham Shensie

characters.name: Twilight Secret Sect Head

characters.description: The Twilight Secret Sect's best one-on-one fighter, chosen to join the delegation sent to meet the Raven Sect.
characters.name: Twilight Secret Sect Duelist

characters.description: The former sect duelist, now head of the Twilight Secret Sect and leader of its surviving disciples. Bereaved and inexperienced in large-scale war, she must prepare the frightened survivors for the campaign against the Raven Sect.
characters.name: New Twilight Secret Sect Head

characters.description: A Twilight Secret Sect fighter selected to join the delegation sent to meet the Raven Sect.
characters.name: Patrol Captain

characters.description: The patrol captain is revealed to be Desert Mirage, the same person also called Shock. His attachment to the Twilight Secret Sect remains central after earlier losses.
characters.name: Desert Mirage

characters.description: An expelled former member of the Twilight Secret Sect who can suppress Hadjar's awareness of the imprisoned Black General by touching him.
characters.name: Guy

characters.description: The imprisoned source of the soul fragment carried by Hadjar, as identified through Twilight Secret Sect records. His connection to Hadjar increases the political danger surrounding the Raven Sect negotiations.
characters.name: Black General

characters.description: A self-modified warrior alchemist who speaks for the Raven Sect before its assembled army. He studies Hadjar's unusually altered blood and offers answers about Hadjar's origins in exchange for allegiance.
characters.name: Raven Sect Commander

characters.description: One of the few people in Hadjar's company whom Abraham considers to have meaningful experience of war. He remains with the group as the Twilight Secret Sect prepares for a siege and Hadjar is pressed to assume command.
characters.name: Alba Udun

characters.description: Hadjar's young mage companion, able to unravel a major Therna construction with a few words and little power. His unusual command of magic makes him valuable as the sect improvises its defenses.
characters.name: The Lesket Mage

characters.description: An experienced archer whom Hadjar trusts to command the Twilight Secret Sect's archers and artillery. He accepts the battlefield assignment and restrains an impulsive opening attack as the Raven Sect deploys its siege engines.
characters.name: Gustaf

characters.description: The ancient guardian of the Twilight Mountains and a former soldier of the Black General. It freezes the battlefield and places a Therna mark on Hadjar.
characters.name: Twilight Mountains' Guardian Spirit

characters.description: The Twilight Secret Sect's chief smith, who accepts responsibility for a disciple's secret weapons dealings and explains how an anti-spirit golem could threaten the guardian.
characters.name: Chief Blacksmith

characters.description: A youthful but immensely powerful wizard serving as an adviser to the human army in the distant past.
characters.name: The Potter

characters.description: The historical name by which the Black General is known in the Potter's era. The Potter recognizes the connection after hearing Hadjar's full name and warns him that the name carries a dangerous association in this time.
characters.name: Black God

characters.description: The Winter Court aristocrat who rules the Rainbow Elves in the era of the Potter's siege. A curse makes her resemble each observer's beloved, and she asks Hadjar to save her daughter if her people cannot be spared.
characters.name: Fae Queen

characters.description: The title used for Hadjar by the human king during the Potter's historical campaign. The king notices his swordsmanship and recognizes him as the northerner summoned into the army's decisive siege.
characters.name: Wind of the Northern Valleys

characters.description: The child Hadjar promised the Fae Queen he would protect. He finds her during the fall of the fae castle and rescues her from the human king, after which the guardian spirit identifies her as a future warrior queen.
characters.name: Fae Queen's Daughter

characters.description: A Twilight Secret Sect defender fighting in the outer battle after the Raven cannon breaches the castle. She stands among Hadjar's allies as the sect struggles to keep the invaders from its hidden artifact.
characters.name: Itia

characters.description: A dangerous demon whom Hadjar summons because his knowledge may reveal the Raven Sect's hiding place. He returns mutilated from the Summer Queen's realm, restores his body with darkness, and offers cooperation on his own terms.
characters.name: Lord of Nightmares

characters.description: The terminally ill elder who leads the concealed mountain community controlling the Therna accumulators Hadjar needs. Though he appears mortal and has no detectable energy, his presence immediately puts Hadjar on guard.
characters.name: Hidden-Mountain Community Leader

characters.description: A spirit who appears within Hadjar's recovered childhood memory during the ice-lake trial. He offers to help Hadjar rediscover the true name of the North.
characters.name: Ice-Wolf Chief

characters.description: The Raven master's disciple who leads a delegation from the island castle. He recognizes Hadjar as another bearer of a Black General soul fragment and refuses the invading army's demand for surrender.
characters.name: Raven Master's Leading Disciple

characters.name: Raven Master

characters.description: The man who raised or trained Hadjar, now revealed as a soul golem engineered and controlled by the Raven master. The memories returned by his death retain an attachment to Hadjar that interferes with the master's ritual.
characters.name: Hadjar's Former Master

characters.description: The principal magic specialist on the Twilight Secret Sect council, recognizable by his tattoos and staff.
characters.name: Chief Mage

characters.description: The ruler in the sect chronicle of the Potter-era siege. He commands the human attackers, kills the fae king, and is later imprisoned with his servant.
characters.name: Human King

characters.name: Ancient King

characters.description: The ancient king's servant, connected to Abraham Shensie's companion through a distant spiritual or family bond associated with their earlier anomaly expedition.
characters.name: Ancient King's Servant

characters.description: An officer in the invading force who works with Alba Udun to coordinate artillery and field fortifications outside the Raven Sect castle.
characters.name: Unnamed Officer

recaps.ending: The coalition's invasion of the Raven Sect's artificial anomaly ends with the deaths of the Raven master's leading disciple and the Raven master. Lathea kills the disciple, and the lingering attachment within Hadjar's former master briefly restrains the Raven master so Hadjar can strike the killing blow. The collapsing anomaly releases the Black General, who leaves Hadjar unable to remember their final exchange and burdened with more soul fragments. The survivors return to the Strangelands and bury their dead. Itia, permanently maimed, remains as archivist of the Twilight Secret Sect. Hadjar leaves for the northern lands with Lathea, Alba Udun, the Lesket mage, and an unnamed officer under the squad name Heaven Foxes. The immediate Raven Sect war is finished, but the Black General is free, the Soul Stone remains beyond Hadjar's reach, the Lord of Nightmares is still owed one request, and the power of the North continues to exact a cost from Hadjar's soul.
recaps.in_short: Detained by the Twilight Secret Sect as a Raven Sect army approaches, Hadjar earns command and organizes an improvised defense. A failed mission through the guardian spirit's time anomaly sends him and Desert Mirage into the past, where Hadjar helps breach a fae castle but saves the Fae Queen's daughter before returning. The Raven commander steals the Soul Stone, kills many defenders, and leaves the sect ruined. Hadjar learns that the Black General created Therna but seeks the world's destruction, gains a route to the hidden Raven Sect, survives a northern trial, and awakens the true name of the North. He then assembles a coalition and invades the Raven Sect's artificial anomaly. Lathea kills the enemy's leading disciple, while Hadjar kills the Raven master after learning that his former master was a soul golem. The Black General is freed as the anomaly collapses and erases Hadjar's memory of their exchange. After burying the fallen, Hadjar and four companions form the Heaven Foxes and depart north.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar Darkhan, known as the Mad General and the Wind of the Northern Valleys, carried a fragment of the imprisoned Black General's soul and travelled with trusted companions including Lathea, Alba Udun, Abraham Shensie, Guy, and a young mage. His path had repeatedly drawn him through war, supernatural bargains, and displacements in time. The Lord of Nightmares had become both a dangerous ally and a source of unresolved debts. Hadjar also owed promised songs to the beast of swamps and bogs, which had granted him a reprieve of one year and one day before beginning its hunt. As the new journey begins, these obligations remain open while Hadjar and his companions become involved in a conflict between the Twilight Secret Sect and its Raven adversaries.

Hadjar's party is detained by the Twilight Secret Sect just as the Raven Sect demands negotiations. Abraham Shensie, a former sect master, argues that Hadjar may be able to locate the enemy's hidden base. The Raven emissary studies Hadjar's altered blood, offers knowledge of his origins in exchange for allegiance, and is refused. Evidence points to a dangerous artifact in the sect vault as the true object of the siege. Abraham also reveals that he seeks immortality and has a troubled history with the sect's finest duelist. With the sect's cultivators powerful but untrained for war, Abraham presses Hadjar to take command. The sect head makes authority conditional on a restricted duel. Hadjar defeats the duelist through physical skill without injuring her, proving the discipline of his sword style. At the end of the contest, the sect head gives him the general's medallion and orders the sect to obey him.

Hadjar finds the Twilight Secret Sect poorly supplied and reorganizes its defenses around practical weapons, sentries, archers, and small frontline units. Lathea commits to stand with him, while Gustaf receives command of the bows and artillery. The Raven Sect arrives with mercenaries, siege towers, mortars, Therna cannons, and other specialized engines. The Twilight Mountains' guardian spirit freezes the battlefield and warns that the Raven commander carries a casket able to kill the mountains. It then isolates the castle inside a time anomaly. The reprieve may last days, but an anti-spirit golem could shorten it to hours, and the Raven cannons can destroy the castle in two salvos. Because the contested artifact cannot be removed and would threaten the mortal world if captured, Hadjar abandons the idea of a static defense. He proposes crossing the active time boundary and destroying the enemy artillery before the anomaly fails.

The Lesket mage explains that crossing the guardian spirit's boundary requires a constructed bridge through unstable layers of time and space. Hadjar and Desert Mirage accept the danger. Lathea becomes the stationary anchor, while the two fighters must cross with almost no equipment and destroy the Raven artillery within minutes. If both leave the bridge, or if the guardian falls, the spell could kill everyone involved and destroy the mountains. The mage completes the path, but the journey immediately becomes unstable. A fragment of broken reality tears away part of the bridge, and Desert Mirage saves Hadjar from the rupture. The resulting wave throws both travelers into the anomaly before they reach the Raven camp. Their carefully timed sabotage mission ends with them lost beyond the collapsed route, while Lathea and the threatened sect remain behind.

Hadjar and Desert Mirage awaken in weaker mortal bodies and discover that the anomaly has sent them into the distant past. They enter a human army preparing to besiege the castle of the Rainbow Elves, a campaign tied to the legendary Potter. Posing as mercenaries, they seek a way into the castle and hope its guardian can return them home. Their cover nearly fails at an officers' council, but the Potter claims them as assistants. He recognizes them as future travelers and believes their arrival was foretold. Hadjar's name also leads him to connect the Black General with the historical title Black God. The Potter cannot be assured of his own future success, but he offers the displaced pair a bargain: help him seize the dangerous artifact guarded by the Rainbow Elves, and he will send them back to their own time. With no other route home, Hadjar accepts.

The Fae Queen secretly approaches Hadjar and asks him to save her daughter if the Potter's siege cannot be stopped. When the human assault begins, Hadjar takes command of nearby soldiers, defeats a winged counterattack, secures a crossing over the moat, and shields a siege tower from massed arrows. He completes a new sword stance and opens the castle gates, allowing the human army inside. The breach draws him toward the Fae Queen's daughter as her parents face the human king. Hadjar realizes that the queen's need to save her child was the force that pulled him and Desert Mirage through time. He breaks the Potter's restraint and carries the girl out through a tower window. The Fae Queen's spell returns him to the present, and the dying guardian spirit identifies the rescued child as a future warrior queen. Hadjar arrives beside the spirit with the Raven commander waiting for him.

The guardian spirit gives Hadjar enough frozen time to destroy most of the Raven cannons and escape the temporal rift with Desert Mirage. One cannon survives. Abraham then admits that he altered the sect chronicles and reveals a connection to the ancient king from the Potter's war. The remaining cannon breaches the castle, and Raven fighters pour inside while Hadjar's blade absorbs soul fragments from those he kills. In the hidden chamber, the defenders confront the Raven commander over the Soul Stone. The ancient king's identity manifests through Abraham and explains that the artifact spiritually joins related travelers, and Hadjar concludes that the Raven Sect intends to use it to restore the Black General. The commander sacrifices followers and his own arm to summon a fragment of the Verge, overwhelms the defenders, and takes the stone. He spares Hadjar on his master's orders and escapes. The imprisoned Black General refuses to explain why he warned Hadjar never to touch the Soul Stone.

The Twilight castle is left ruined. Abraham ends the mortally wounded sect head's suffering, Gustaf is dead, Lathea is badly injured, and Alba Udun has lost his sight and part of his energy body. Gustaf's death reveals that he was Itia's son. Hadjar turns the survivors toward a new war before the Raven Sect can use the Soul Stone at the next full moon. To locate the hidden enemy, he summons the Lord of Nightmares. The demon produces an object made by an ancient wizard, and Hadjar's blood unlocks memories of the Black General. They show that the general created Therna for mortals but ultimately planned to destroy the Nameless World.

The new Twilight Secret Sect head begins adapting from bereaved duelist to leader of the surviving disciples. The Lesket mage studies the portal scroll and determines that it needs Therna accumulators; without them, roughly two hundred people would be consumed to power it. Lathea leaves to support coalition-building in her homeland, while Hadjar, Alba Udun, and a sect representative search the northern mountains for a hidden community descended from an earlier anti-Raven campaign. The community admits Hadjar through an energyless barrier after judging him distinct from the Black General's followers. Local magic allows him to survive where normal cultivation and artifacts fail. Inside, a concentrated Therna star strengthens his body. He then meets the hidden community's leader, an apparently mortal and terminally ill elder whose undetectable power and unexplained knowledge make Hadjar immediately wary. The accumulators remain conditional on what the leader demands.

The hidden leader refuses political support but offers Hadjar the needed Therna accumulators if he survives a night naked in an ice-lake anomaly. The lake strips away power, memory, and identity, forcing Hadjar to relive a childhood assassination attempt by his uncle. Within that memory, the ice-wolf chief helps him recover the true name of the North. Hadjar learns that the Lord of Nightmares intervened during the attack, altered his uncle's intentions, and suppressed the northern power before it could bind the boy to the Winter Queen. Hadjar emerges able to wield the North's essence, though it leaves lasting pain in his soul. He confronts the demon, ends their friendship, preserves only one promised request, and declares his intention to kill him someday. After the ordeal, the hidden leader honors the bargain and gives Hadjar the accumulators, while still refusing to bring him before the secluded factions' council.

Hadjar rejoins the Twilight Secret Sect survivors and Abraham's squad on the way to the regional gathering hosted in Lathea's homeland. Nearly eighteen thousand fighters assemble for the anti-Raven campaign. Abraham argues that the delegates have already chosen war, presents the portal plan, and nominates Hadjar to command. Hadjar proves his fitness in a public duel, drawing first blood from Abraham while demonstrating better control of the North's power despite the damage it still causes him. Lathea directs the organization of the mixed force, Alba Udun converts cannons to use Therna, and the Lesket mage studies the portal apparatus. Abraham also links the portal's creator to experiments with anomalies and routes beyond sealed reality. By the end of the preparations, the mage has learned how to open the portal. The coalition now has an army, artillery, an energy source, and a working path to the Raven Sect.

The Lesket mage determines that the Raven castle occupies a stable artificial anomaly beyond ordinary world-roads. The portal's landing point cannot be predicted, but Hadjar commits the expedition and the entire force is transported to the rocky island holding the castle. The anomaly contains no World River energy, forcing the invaders to rely on personal reserves and Therna. A narrow bridge appears to make a direct assault impossible, and the Raven master's leading disciple refuses surrender. Hadjar answers with a layered siege plan. Artillery and archers will occupy the walls while an officer leads five hundred fighters through northern sewers. Alba Udun will place linked charges to damage the lower structures and alter the water pressure, flooding the castle's lower levels. Hadjar then intends to cross in a siege tower, establish a courtyard battle, and open routes for attacks from three directions. The assault must begin before the defenders close the infiltration route.

The Raven bridge expands and releases thousands of swordsmen, exposing the apparent chokepoint as a trap. Hadjar's shield lines suffer heavy losses but hold while artillery forces the defenders to spend their limited power. He drives the army into a prolonged melee and expends much of his remaining strength to kill hundreds, buying time for the infiltration group. The Raven master's leading disciple then challenges the depleted Hadjar. Their related wind-and-sword techniques reveal their shared Black General lineage. Hadjar turns back a major attack, but the disciple survives by sacrificing an artifact and gains the advantage. Lathea intervenes and kills him in retribution for Gustaf and the other dead. Hadjar's sword absorbs the disciple's soul and fragment, triggering a vast Therna eruption that destabilizes the anomaly. Swept underwater and separated from the battle, Hadjar awakens helpless before the man he recognizes as his master.

The Raven master reveals that Hadjar's former master was a soul golem engineered to locate bearers of Black General fragments. He prepares to remove Hadjar's heart, replace it with the cursed stone, and use the gathered fragments to restore the Black General. An ancient king and servant interrupt but are defeated. The remaining attachment within Hadjar's former master then manifests through the Raven master's body and restrains him long enough for Hadjar to reclaim his power and kill him. As the anomaly collapses, the Black General appears free of his chains, warns that Hadjar has absorbed too many fragments, and causes him to forget their exchange. Back in the Strangelands, the survivors hold a mass funeral. The maimed Itia remains as the Twilight Secret Sect's archivist. Hadjar, Lathea, Alba Udun, the Lesket mage, and an unnamed officer form the Heaven Foxes and depart toward the northern lands. The Raven campaign is over, but the freed Black General, the missing Soul Stone, the demon's debt, and the cost of the North remain unresolved.

recaps.ending: Hadjar enters the Twilight Secret Sect after the mountain spirit keeps him on the Twilight Path for three weeks. Desert Mirage survives their duel and warns Hadjar to leave, but Hadjar instead offers him a place with the group. At the council, Abraham Shensie offers the key and knowledge of Therna as payment for sect leadership in a campaign against the Raven Sect. He also publicly identifies Hadjar as the Black General's supposed descendant and disciple, without Hadjar's consent. The five sect chiefs remain divided, and the claim is still untested when a wounded scout arrives. At least two thousand Raven Sect swordsmen are only one day south. Hadjar, Lathea, the recovering Lesket mage, Abraham's squad, Desert Mirage, and the new Lesket leadership are alive. The sect's alliance decision and the approaching battle remain immediate, while Hadjar still owes the Black General an unspecified favor and faces the beast of swamps and bogs after its one-year-and-one-day reprieve.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar enters the spirit world with the Lord of Nightmares to save the wounded Lesket mage, confronting the Summer Queen's influence over his past and accepting a future debt to the Black General. He bargains with a primeval god, crosses hostile spirit lands, defeats his white-dragon ancestor, and returns with the thorn that heals the mage. Lathea escapes the winter queen's wolves, and the group survives the wolf alpha when the northerner forces the pack away. The Lesket patriarch's plot against his youngest son collapses; Lathea kills him, and his elder son takes command. Farther south, Hadjar reunites with Abraham Shensie's squad, defeats but saves Desert Mirage, and passes the Twilight Secret Sect's mountain trial. Abraham asks the sect to lead a war against the Raven Sect and uses Hadjar's connection to the Black General as leverage. Before the council decides, a scout reports that a large Raven Sect force is one day away.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar traveled with Lathea and a young Lesket mage while pursuing his conflict with the Raven Sect. His path had also tied him to Therna, the winter queen, the Lord of Nightmares, and a dangerous presence within his soul.

Hadjar wakes badly injured in a northerner's shelter. The Lesket mage has kept him alive but is dying from a soul wound, while Lathea is imprisoned by the winter queen's wolves. The northerner directs Hadjar to find a cure in the Summer Queen's palace, and the Lord of Nightmares accompanies him into the spirit world to collect an old debt. After evading winter guards, they enter a forest that exposes wounds of the soul. Hadjar relives his regrets over Ina and the cruelty that helped shape him as the Mad General. The Summer Queen then claims that Ina and another woman from his past were free-willed fragments of herself. Enraged and distrustful, Hadjar defeats three Summer Court knights. The Lord of Nightmares denies knowing the truth about those fragments, and Hadjar continues toward the palace with Ina's pendant, unwilling to treat fate or either queen as the master of his choices.

The Mirage and Dream Forest demands blood for every step and attacks Hadjar with false visions. An Angler of Truth redirects him toward the ancestral rock where the white dragon waits. Flower spirits agree to guide him only if he removes the primeval beast of swamps and bogs from their land. Unable to defeat the god, Hadjar exploits its hunger for remembrance. He promises future songs, gains a reprieve of one year and one day, and persuades it to move elsewhere, though it vows to hunt him when the term ends. The flower spirits then trap the Lord of Nightmares in Hadjar's shadow under their hospitality rules. During their celebration, a flower warrior challenges Hadjar to a ceremonial sword dance because of the Black General's connection to her family. The imprisoned being in Hadjar's soul offers power in exchange for an undefined future favor. Hadjar accepts, entering both the duel and a new obligation.

A memory shows the Black General killing the flower warrior's mother during an ancient campaign against the spirit realm. Borrowed Therna strengthens Hadjar for the duel, but the flower warrior remains superior and intends to destroy the fragment within him. Sunrise ends the contest under the village's hospitality law, allowing Hadjar to escape with the promised route map. He then witnesses the Lord of Nightmares and the Black General acknowledge old oaths and former enmity. The demon confirms that he brought Hadjar into this world, but says an oath prevents further explanation. Elsewhere, the Summer Queen asks her sister to block Hadjar's route and seeks support for a larger supernatural war, but the winter queen refuses. At the Spirit Bowls, Hadjar evades their red-armored guardian, uses the Black General's Verge warrior meditation to absorb natural energy, and advances his cultivation. His sharper perception lets him identify weaknesses within techniques. After a restrained duel at the highest bowl, he flies beyond the guardian and reaches the ancestral rock.

At the ancestral rock, the white dragon reveals himself as Hadjar's ancestor and the last spirit of their bloodline. His memories show that the god of wisdom made him a disciple, that he later fought beside the being now confined within Hadjar, and that both defended the worlds against creatures beyond the Verge. The ancestor identifies that being as his second master and begins an inheritance duel. Hadjar is initially overwhelmed. The Black General teaches him to use Therna directly through his body and outlines a path from sword techniques toward a personal law. Applying that lesson, Hadjar creates Headwind, defeats the white dragon, and receives the dying spirit's feathered wings. The inheritance becomes a body pattern capable of producing real wings once. With the ancestral rock collapsing, Hadjar races toward the Summer Court capital, carrying the power needed for the next stage of his rescue.

Hadjar crosses the ancestor lake and reaches the Summer Court capital during its solstice festival. The Summer Queen attempts to contain him through court hospitality, but the Lord of Nightmares confronts her and sends Hadjar into the treasury. Hadjar takes a thorn and returns to the mountains while the demon remains behind to fight. The northerner applies the thorn to the Lesket mage, ending his fever and leaving him with an ancient blessing. Lathea then reaches the shelter alive but severely injured after escaping the wolves, and Hadjar stabilizes her. The northerner explains that the true North lies beyond ordinary navigation and gives Hadjar a blank map governed by ancient magic. While gathering firewood, Hadjar meets a forest master and learns more about northern customs. A wolfman connected to the pursuing pack approaches, reveals knowledge of Hadjar's enchanted protection and the Black General, and invokes a binding northern convention before demanding answers about Lathea.

The wolfman admits that the winter queen ordered Lathea's abduction. Hadjar's evasive answer sends him racing toward the northerner's hut, where the wolf pack gathers. The wolf alpha demands Lathea and reopens a century-old grievance over the death of the northerner's brother. With Lathea freezing inside, the Lesket mage secretly strengthens Hadjar's connection to northern wind so he can challenge the alpha. Hadjar draws first blood but cannot overcome the alpha's darkness domain. The northerner intervenes after gaining the Rule of the Axe, kills an attacking wolf, and forces the pack to withdraw without settling their feud. A messenger then summons him back to the North. Before leaving, he gives Hadjar a small item. Hadjar realizes that the Lesket patriarch sent the expedition to locate a northern native and force him home. The mage admits his father's plan, rejects it despite likely exile, and joins Hadjar's party with Lathea's support.

Lathea explains that the wolves suppressed her cultivation until an unexplained golden flash restored it, enabling her escape. Hadjar, Lathea, and the recovering mage descend from the mountains and encounter more than twelve hundred Lesket warriors. Hadjar concludes that the patriarch designed the mission to kill his youngest son and manipulate the elder heir. The elder son turns the soldiers against their father and exposes the patriarch's murder of a newborn daughter because of a prophecy. The mage unleashes ancient magic but stops before killing himself. When the patriarch later attacks Lathea, the mage takes the blow and Lathea kills the old clan head. The elder son succeeds him and commits the Lesket force to accompany negotiations with the Twilight Secret Sect. Lathea cares for the injured mage but tells Hadjar that she considers him a loyal friend rather than a romantic partner. The three companions then travel west to meet Abraham Shensie's group and continue preparations against the Raven Sect.

Hadjar, Lathea, and the Lesket mage reach a border market hosting the Fall Twilight Festival. They reunite with Abraham Shensie, Alba Udun, Guy, Gustaf, and Itia. Abraham's operation is so risky that Hadjar withholds the Lord of Nightmares' role when recounting his recent journey. A festival legend describes the Lord of Nightmares freeing an imprisoned king after the Black General's soul was scattered, but the tale's historical accuracy remains uncertain. The festival tournament offers Therna knowledge and entry to the Twilight Secret Sect. Hundreds compete through a physical-strength test and lethal battles against magical incarnations until only twenty remain. Abraham's actual objective requires another route into the sect. After the final contest, he publicly questions why the sect risked outsiders while withholding its own disciples, then names Hadjar and provokes a direct challenge from Desert Mirage, Hadjar's former acquaintance from the Sea of Sand.

Desert Mirage accepts the public duel while privately remembering an earlier promise to fight Hadjar. Although the sect disciple has higher cultivation, Hadjar breaks his wolf-shaped saber attack by disturbing the Therna that sustains it. Desert Mirage activates a flame amulet that begins destroying him from within. Hadjar defeats him, then forces the watching sect master to provide treatment. The master takes Desert Mirage's place, but an apparent summons from the mountain ends her attack. She identifies herself as the Sea Whisper and invites Hadjar's group into the sect as guests. The mountain rejects Hadjar's wind path and drops the party into its foothills. Alba Udun senses that the mountain itself is ancient and conscious. Hadjar enters the Twilight Path alone and sees a vision of the Lord of Nightmares tending an unidentified prisoner in a chained crystal sarcophagus. He emerges three weeks later, after his companions, and learns that the mountain spirit decides who may pass. Desert Mirage has survived.

Desert Mirage escorts Hadjar to the Twilight Secret Sect's council and advises him to leave. Hadjar instead offers him a place with the group if he abandons the sect. Abraham Shensie asks the sect to lead a campaign against the Raven Sect, offering the key and knowledge of Therna as payment. The five chiefs disagree, while the sect head argues that Abraham's roughly fifteen hundred fighters cannot strike an enemy whose headquarters remains hidden. Without Hadjar's consent, Abraham presents him as the Black General's descendant and disciple and calls that connection the campaign's missing advantage. The sect head proposes testing the claim before committing. The debate is overtaken by a wounded scout, who reports that at least two thousand black-cloaked Raven Sect swordsmen killed his companions and are only one day south. The council has not decided, but the enemy's approach makes the alliance and coming battle immediate.
